capabilities.capability: MDBList HTTP Client with Rate Limiting & Retry
capabilities.source_behavior: Custom HTTP client with per-key rate limiting (429 handling, X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset), retry-once on 401 (token refresh), exponential backoff for 5xx, configurable retry-safe for GET requests, scope-based checkScope injection for cancellation. OkHttp engine with redirect disabled, size-limited response body, suspendCancellableCoroutine.

capabilities.source_behavior: Dual-mode ratings: API key (unauthenticated) OR authenticated account-based. Supports single and batch media queries. Batches up to 200 IDs with 50ms debounce window. 30-minute cache TTL. Returns MDBListRatings domain model with IMDB, TMDB, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, Trakt, Letterboxd, Audience, MAL ratings. Also includes MDBListRepository for settings-integrated access.
capabilities.target_behavior: EXISTS but limited: Only API-key-based ratings (no authenticated account fallback). No batch rating support. Simple per-request cache (not batched/debounced). Ratings returned as MetaExternalRating list (not MDBListRatings domain model). Settings have per-provider toggles and sync support. Platform-specific storage via expect/actual (NSUserDefaults for iOS, SharedPreferences for Android).

risks: MDBList API rate limits (reference handles with per-key rate limiting, retry-after, exponential backoff) - target must implement similar in MdbListHttpClient
MDBList OAuth scope invalidation on profile change (reference uses scope generation tracking with CancellationException for stale operations) - critical for multi-profile correctness
MDBList sync journal has 30-day retention - after that a full sync is required; target must implement the same watermark/expiry logic
MDBList API returns IDs in multiple schemes (IMDB, TMDB, TVDB, Trakt, MDBList) - cross-referencing via MdbListMediaIndex is essential for correct projection
Write-after-read consistency for scrobble (reference implements mergeFetchedPlayback to prefer local writes over stale server state) - must be ported
Target's Continue Watching enrichment cache is per-source (WatchProgressSource-scoped) - MDBLIST must be added as a new source scope
Target's Trakt and Simkl integrations serve as the pattern for MDBList parity - not re-inventing the architecture is critical
MDBList client ID is sensitive - must be in config/BuildConfig, not hardcoded
iOS Keychain vs Android ProtectedProfilePreferences - expect/actual pattern already established for Trakt and Simkl auth storage
